quizzes.title: Getting Started Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Introduction & JSX, Components & Props, State & Events.

options: A programming language that replaces JavaScript
A JavaScript library for building user interfaces
questions.explanation: React is a JavaScript library that builds user interfaces from components. It is written in JavaScript, not a replacement for it.

questions.prompt: What does this component show in the browser?
questions.explanation: Curly braces run a JavaScript expression, so 3 + 4 is calculated and 7 is shown.

questions.prompt: What does this code show inside the page?
options: An error, because children is not allowed
questions.explanation: Text between the tags is passed as children. The Card prints the title prop and then the children.

questions.prompt: A button has onClick. Which version is correct?
questions.explanation: onClick needs a function. The correct line passes an arrow function. Calling setCount directly would run during rendering.

questions.prompt: Complete the hook call that creates state with the starting value 0.
questions.explanation: useState(0) creates a state variable with the first value 0 and returns the value and its setter.

questions.prompt: Why should you not write items.push("x") on a state array?
options: React only sees a change when you set a new array, so push may not update the screen
push is not allowed in JavaScript
State arrays must have only one item
questions.explanation: Mutating state in place does not tell React to re-render. Create a new array, such as [...items, "x"], and pass it to the setter.

quizzes.title: Hooks & Data Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Lists, Keys & Conditional Rendering, Forms & Controlled Inputs, useEffect & Fetching Data.

options: Three list items: A, B, C
questions.explanation: map turns each letter into an li element, so three items are shown. Each has its own key.

questions.prompt: What is the best key for items in a list loaded from a database?
options: The unique id of each record
The same number for all items
questions.explanation: Keys must be unique and stable. A database id stays the same for the same record. Random keys change on every render.

questions.prompt: What is shown when count is 0?
questions.explanation: With && a falsy left side is returned as it is. The number 0 is displayed by React, so use count > 0 && ...

questions.prompt: Complete the handler so the page does not reload when the form is submitted.
questions.explanation: e.preventDefault() stops the browser default of reloading the page on submit.

questions.prompt: An input has value={name} but no onChange. What happens?
options: The input becomes read-only and React warns you
questions.explanation: A controlled input shows the state value. Without onChange nothing updates the state, so typing does nothing.

options: Only when the component is removed
questions.explanation: An empty dependency array means the effect has no dependencies, so it runs once after the first render.

options: Passing data through many levels of components (prop drilling)
questions.explanation: Context makes a value available to all components below a Provider, so you do not pass props through every level.
The closest Provider above the component gives the value dark, so useContext returns dark.

questions.prompt: Complete the name so this function is a valid custom hook.
questions.explanation: A custom hook must have a name that starts with use. Any name like useToggle is accepted.

questions.prompt: Which environment variable can your Vite React code read?
questions.explanation: Vite only exposes variables that start with VITE_. They are read with import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL.

questions.prompt: Which component should you use for an internal link so the page does not reload?
questions.explanation: Link changes the URL and lets the router show the new page without a full reload. Route only describes a page.

questions.prompt: What does the route path /courses/:id do when the address is /courses/7?
options: useParams gives id with the value "7"
questions.explanation: The part starting with a colon is a parameter. useParams returns it, and URL parameters are always strings.
